issues.legal_issue: A person who purchases land after public notice of its acquisition is not competent to challenge the acquisition proceedings.
material_facts: The land had been notified for acquisition before the appellants purchased it through later sale deeds.
The appellants sought to challenge the acquisition after purchasing the land.
issues.conclusion: The appellants, as subsequent purchasers, could not challenge the acquisition proceedings and could claim no title-based relief against the acquisition.
issues.legal_principle: A purchaser who deals with land after publication of a notification under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 does so at their own peril. The purchase does not bind the State or acquisition beneficiary; the purchaser may at most claim compensation through the vendor's title. The Court relied on Pandit Leela Ram v. Union of India, Sneh Prabha v. State of Uttar Pradesh, Union of India v. Shri Shiv Kumar Bhargava, U.P. Jal Nigam v. Kalra Properties, Star Wire (India) Ltd. v. State of Haryana, Ajay Kishan Singhal v. Union of India, Mahavir v. Rural Institute, Gian Chand v. Gopala, Meera Sahni v. Lieutenant Governor of Delhi, and Tika Ram v. State of U.P.

predicates.acquisition_challenge_proceeding: A person seeks judicial relief challenging proceedings to acquire land.
predicates.purchase_after_public_acquisition_notice: The person acquired the land after public notice that it was required for acquisition.

issues.definition: When a person seeks to challenge an acquisition after acquiring the land following public notice of the acquisition, the person cannot challenge the acquisition.
